items.title: Brain Moves Its Touch Center to Keep Feeling Sensation
items.snippet: Why does artificial touch fade over time? Penn State engineers used fNIRS brain imaging to solve sensory habituation during transcutaneous nerve stimulation, discovering a 5-second pulse protocol that maintains a stable sense of touch while the brain recruits distributed networks.

items.title: Why Nervous System Hyperarousal Keeps Jolting You Awake
items.snippet: Ever jolt awake with a racing heart just as you drift off? A study in PLOS Mental Health reveals that frequent hypnic jerks—or sleep starts—are not simple muscle twitches, but markers of anxiety, insomnia severity, and nervous system hyperarousal.

items.title: Multiple Sclerosis Atrophy Spreads From High-Stress Neural Hubs
items.snippet: Why does brain volume loss in multiple sclerosis follow distinct patterns? An MRI study of 2,187 patients reveals that atrophy originates in metabolically exhausted network hubs—including the thalamus and sensorimotor cortices—spreading outward along structural connections.

items.title: Daytime Sleep Waves in Parkinson’s Linked to Hallucinations
items.snippet: When sleep invades wakefulness: An EEG study of 84 Parkinson’s patients reveals that sleep-like slow brain waves intrude into daytime consciousness, directly tracking with hallucinations and cognitive decline while offering a potential prodromal biomarker.
